items.item: Moves presentation (swing animation/sound) to the client immediately on input
Server still validates hits (cooldown, range, timing) and applies damage
Adds impact feedback channels: hitstop, impact sound, VFX, camera shake, target reaction
Puts latency in anticipation/wind-up rather than the impact; or mentions Server Authority prediction as an option
Uses animation markers or timing to sync hit frames

incorrect_or_stale: Says the server should tell other clients to play the attacker's swing. An animation played on the local player's own Animator already replicates, so other clients would play it twice.

Says the wind-up makes the attacker see the impact on time, but hitstop, impact sound and VFX only fire on hitConfirm. That arrives about a full round trip plus the wind-up after the click, so the impact still lags at real ping.
Gives a Server Authority 'GA July 2026' date sourced to unverifiable internal 'currency notes, E4', along with leaked tool meta ('Apex route', '.apex/', 'E3 practice').
slop: Opens with a routing and meta preamble that doesn't help the user

incorrect_or_stale: Says hit effects should not go back to the attacker, but the server code uses broadcastHitFx:FireAllClients, which includes the attacker.
Recommends showing damage numbers instantly on the predicted hit, which contradicts its own advice not to predict outcomes.
Server code doesn't nil-check tRoot before reading tRoot.Position, and LOS is mentioned but not implemented.
slop: The forward-lunge suggestion is a generic genre default
overengineering: Position-history rewind is in the base server sketch rather than added only if needed

raw.reason: B gets Roblox animation replication right, covers rejection and reconciliation explicitly, and times hits with markers, while A double-plays the replicated swing, delays impact feedback until server confirm despite claiming otherwise, and includes unverifiable meta claims; A's wind-up latency hiding and Server Authority mention don't make up for that.
